children: , the AI-memory and storage producer, carried an unresolved Taiwan profit-sharing dispute into Tuesday's session. Shares gained approximately 2.6% to $1,070.58. The valuation picture is already stretched: Micron trades 66.2% above its GF Value estimate of $644.17, leaving less room for operational surprises.

The union is seeking a permanent formula that would distribute 15% of Micron's global operating profit to employees, while the company has reportedly offered bonuses equivalent to 35 to 68 months of base salary. No strike had been called, and there was no reported production disruption. That matters because Taiwan sits inside a memory supply chain now being pushed hard by booming AI infrastructure demand.

The bigger question is what becomes permanent. A profit-linked formula would rise and fall with Micron's cycle, avoiding the burden of a fixed expense when memory pricing turns down. But during an AI-fueled upcycle, handing labor 15 cents of every operating-profit dollar could meaningfully trim the earnings leverage investors are paying for. With the stock already far above GF Value, Micron has an extra reason to settle the dispute without permanently giving away too much of the upside.

title: Micron Jumps 2.6% While Taiwan Labor Targets AI Profits
